Subject: Kepler reserved GPU pool — performance spike, interim remediation & next steps

Hi Kevin —

Quick note to acknowledge we saw the latency spike and intermittent 503s on your reserved GPU pool starting ~08:50 PDT this morning. We immediately opened an incident and our SREs are investigating.

What we know so far:
- Impact: increased p90/p99 token latency and transient 503 responses for a subset of Kepler hosts in us-west-2 reserved pool.
- Scope: affects roughly 12% of your requests routed to the reserved nodes between 08:50–09:12; remainder of requests routed normally.
- Short-term mitigation: we enabled degraded-mode routing (route to warm-standby variants) and temporarily increased out-of-band capacity for your pool to reduce latency spikes.

Immediate next steps (we own these):
1) SREs will collect allocator + kernel metrics and an allocator snapshot (ETA: 45–60m).
2) Roll a targeted restart of the allocator on impacted nodes if snapshot shows stuck queues (ETA: 90m).
3) We'll follow up with a post-incident summary and proposed credits within 48 hours.

I realize this is disruptive — apologies for the impact. Marissa is on the thread for any commercial questions; Ben is available for billing/credits conversation. I will update you with root cause and remediation timeline as soon as we have the allocator snapshot.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Kepler reserved GPU pool — allocator snapshot and initial hypothesis

Quick update from SRE run: collected allocator_snapshot and service metrics at 09:22; attaching a trimmed snapshot for the team to review. Preliminary findings:

- Root cause hypothesis: allocator worker threads on a subset of reserved nodes experienced sustained queue-head locking due to an edge-case in cross-tenant scheduling (fairshare reconciliation). This caused a backlog that led to request timeouts and transient 503s.
- Evidence: sustained growth in per-shard queue length, thread stacks showing repeated spin-wait in fairness reconciliation loop. No OOMs or kernel panics observed.
- Immediate remediation performed: targeted allocator restart on 4 affected hosts (completed 10:12), route draining for affected shards and warm-standby routing enabled (09:55–10:30).
- Impact mitigation: the routing change reduced p99 latency to baseline by 10:30.

Attachments: allocator_snapshot_0316.log (text/plain), svc_metrics_0316.csv (text/csv)

Next steps (owners):
- Laura: confirm whether the 03/12 kernel commit could interact with fairness reconciliation (ETA: EOD).
- Eng/SRE: add a guardrail in the allocator to detect runaway fairness reconciliation loops (ETA: patch + canary 72h).
- CS/Sales: draft customer-facing postmortem and credit proposal (Jordan & Ben).

Neha Kapoor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 17 Mar 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: [Update] Kepler reserved GPU pool — interim findings and remediation plan

Kevin / Elena —

Thanks again for patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident update and next steps; full postmortem attached.

Summary (what happened)
- Between 08:50–09:12 PDT on 2028-03-16 a subset of your reserved nodes experienced allocator-level queue locking triggered by a fairness-reconciliation bug. This created a service backlog and transient 503s for ~12% of requests.

What we did (remediation)
- Collected allocator snapshots and metrics (09:22).
- Performed a targeted restart of allocator workers on 4 affected hosts (10:12).
- Activated warm-standby routing and temporary capacity increase to reduce customer-visible errors (09:55–10:30).
- Post-fix: p99 latency returned to baseline and error-rate normalized by 10:45.

Root cause
- An edge-case in the fairness reconciliation path allowed per-tenant queue pointers to spin without progress under a specific request fanout pattern. The code path was exercised by high-concurrency workloads and an uncommon shard boundary condition.

Customer impact & compensation
- Impact window: ~22 minutes (08:50–09:12).
- Estimated affected requests: ~12% of Kepler's traffic to the reserved pool during the window.
- As a gesture of goodwill and to make whole for customer impact, we propose: 30% service credit for March reserved usage applied to your next invoice, pending your acceptance. Ben is available to negotiate if you prefer an alternate arrangement.

Next actions (committed timelines)
- Engineering: guardrail patch + canary deploy (within 72 hours).
- SRE: automated detection for runaway fairness loops (in rollout plan, ETA 7 days).
- Postmortem: full written notes and logs attached — redwood_postmortem_20280316.pdf, allocator_snapshot_0316.log, svc_metrics_0316.csv.
- Meeting: I sent a calendar invite for Tue 2028-03-20 09:00 PDT to review details and any follow-ups.

Links & artifacts
- Postmortem & evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cCqYz-example
- HubSpot case: HS-438192

If you'd like a deeper technical walk-through during the meeting, Laura and Neha will join. Please let me know if the proposed credit is acceptable or if you want to discuss alternate remediation.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
